sensitive_conditions: Uniform convexity modulus must use (2), not merely monotonicity (4) as a definition; source p.4 footnote warns of a different modulus convention.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Deterministic, for every admissible instance and subgradient sequence.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Explicit constants as displayed; no free-cost implementation of prox or linear optimization is inferred.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact bounded objective subgradient observations and exact argmin of a known prox-regularized linear form over Q_R(z). Exact values are available in the source deterministic model but unused by this update.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: Feasible arithmetic mean of x_0,...,x_N; objective gap and rho-th power of norm distance to a localized minimizer.
complexity_scope.regime: As stated in parameter_domains; tuning uses L,R,mu_d,A_d and horizon N. mu_f and rho enter the distance guarantee, not one-stage tuning.
complexity_scope.resource: N subgradient calls and N prox solves generate the output; N=0 outputs z. Forming delta_N additionally requires g_N and maximization of a linear functional over Q_R(z); this certificate is not needed to run the update. The source N convention counts updates, not every certificate operation.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: Selected Algorithm 1 with unit weights and constant beta only.

proofs.locator: p.8 Proposition 1 (14), Lemma 2 and Corollary 1 (16); p.23 Appendix B.2
map: Proposition 1 (14) bounds sum_{i=0}^N <g_i,x_i-x> by beta d_zR(x)+(R^2/(2mu_d beta))sum_{i=0}^N ||g_i||_*^2 for unit weights and constant gains.
Using d_zR<=A_d and ||g_i||_*<=L gives delta_N<=(gamma A_d+L^2 R^2/(2gamma mu_d))/sqrt(N+1).

Appendix B.2 uses <g_i,x_i-x*>>=f(x_i)-f(x*) and <g_i,x_i-x*>>=mu_f||x_i-x*||^rho (the second inequality invokes (4) and constrained optimality). Summing and applying convexity to both f and ||.||^rho gives f(bar_x_N)-f(x*)<=delta_N and mu_f||bar_x_N-x*||^rho<=delta_N.
Corollary 1 substitutes gamma=LR/sqrt(2mu_d A_d), balancing the two terms to obtain (16).

proofs.reading_coverage: Visually checked p.8 statements/formulas and p.23 B.2 in full; definitions and standing assumptions on pp.1,3-7 checked at stated anchors.

assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real normed space; Q is a nonempty closed convex subset. f is subdifferentiable and Lipschitz on Q with all objective subgradients bounded by L in dual norm (Assumption 1).
f satisfies equation (2): for every x,y in Q and a in [0,1], f(a x+(1-a)y)<=a f(x)+(1-a)f(y)-(mu_f/2)a(1-a)[a^(rho-1)+(1-a)^(rho-1)]||x-y||^rho.
d is continuous and mu_d-strongly convex on B={u:||u||<=1}, in convention (2) with rho=2; 0=d(0)<=d(u)<=A_d for every u in B.
Choose z in Q and R>0; x* is a minimizer of f over Q_R(z)=Q intersect B_R(z). Exact objective subgradients and exact localized prox minimization are available.

Use Algorithm 1 with x_0=z, s_0=0, lambda_i=1 and constant beta=gamma sqrt(N+1), gamma=LR/sqrt(2 mu_d A_d). For i=0,...,N-1 query g_i in partial f(x_i), set s_{i+1}=s_i+g_i and x_{i+1}=argmin_{x in Q_R(z)}{<s_{i+1},x-z>+beta d((x-z)/R)}. Output bar_x_N=(sum_{i=0}^N x_i)/(N+1).
statement.conclusion: f(bar_x_N)-f(x*)<=LR sqrt(2A_d/(mu_d(N+1))) and ||bar_x_N-x*||^rho<=(LR/mu_f)sqrt(2A_d/(mu_d(N+1))). Lemma 2's route also bounds ||bar_x_N-x*||^rho<=delta_N/mu_f and delta_N<=LR sqrt(2A_d/(mu_d(N+1))). The optimizer here is for the localized problem; no global-optimum containment is implicit.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Use the primal/dual norm on E/E*. Q_R(z)=Q intersect B_R(z), d_zR(x)=d((x-z)/R). x* minimizes f on Q_R(z); bar_x_N is the arithmetic mean in Algorithm 1. delta_N(z,R)=max_{x in Q_R(z)} (1/(N+1))sum_{i=0}^N <g_i,x_i-x>, with g_i in partial f(x_i). g_N is needed for this analytical gap, even though it is not needed to generate bar_x_N.
statement.parameter_domains: Finite rho in [2,infinity); L,mu_f,mu_d,A_d,R>0; N a nonnegative integer. The prox assumptions imply mu_d<=2A_d. No quadratic growth bound on d is required.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every objective/domain/prox satisfying these assumptions, every center z in Q, every R>0, every integer N>=0 and every admissible exact subgradient sequence. The result is deterministic, with no probability or expectation.
